parts.text: A student investigates the dimensions of a boiling tube. She uses the apparatus shown in Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student pours a small amount of water into the boiling tube and measures the height h 0 from the bench to the initial water level. 2.6 h 0 = ......................................................... cm Suggest one precaution that is taken when measuring the height of the water level to ensure the reading is accurate. You may draw a diagram if it helps your explanation. ................................................................................................................................................... ............................................................................................................................................. [1]

ms.label: 1(a)
ms.text:
precaution for reading water level e.g.:
view scale perpendicularly
rule close to boiling tube
use of set square

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student uses a measuring cylinder graduated in cm 3 to add a volume of water V = 5.0 cm 3 to the boiling tube. Part of the boiling tube, after the water has been added, is shown full size in Fig. 1.2. Fig. 1.2 Measure, and record in the first row of Table 1.1, the new height h of the water level from the bench. [1] Table 1.1 V / cm 3 h / cm H / cm 5.0 10.0 5.5 2.9 15.0 6.7 4.1 20.0 8.3 5.7 25.0 9.6 7.0

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) For the value of V = 5.0 cm 3 , calculate, and record in Table 1.1, the increase in height H of the water in the boiling tube. Use the value of h 0 from (a) , your value of h in Table 1.1 and the equation H = ( h – h 0 ). [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Plot a graph of V / cm 3 ( y -axis) against H / cm ( x -axis). [4]

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
axes labelled with quantity and unit
appropriate scales (occupying at least ½ grid)
plots all correct to ½ small square and precise plots
well-judged line and thin line

parts.label: i
parts.text: (e) (i) Determine the gradient of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. gradient = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 1(e)(i)
ms.text: G present and triangle method shown on graph grid

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate D , the inside diameter of the boiling tube. Use the equation D = 4 G π , where G is numerically equivalent to the gradient in (e)(i) . D = .................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 1(e)(ii)
ms.text: D in range 1.9 cm to 2.4 cm

ms.label: 1(f)
ms.text: inside diameter near base not uniform / owtte

parts.label: g
parts.text: (g) Another student uses this experiment, with the same apparatus, to measure D for a small test-tube of diameter approximately 1.2 cm. He adds water in volumes of 1.0 cm 3 at a time. State and explain one reason why this is not an accurate method to use for this test-tube. ................................................................................................................................................... ............................................................................................................................................. [1]

ms.label: 1(g)
ms.text:
valid critical comment e.g.:
water volumes small – large uncertainty in measuring cylinder
test-tube diameter small – large uncertainty in answer / owtte
height changes small so unreliable
